claims.claim: McCaffery's 1988 printing of the Fifth Head dedication reads 'who one night in 1966 grew me from a bean', where WolfeWiki prints 'who one well-remembered June evening in 1966 grew me from a bean'.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Larry McCaffery, 'On Encompassing the Entire Universe', Science Fiction Studies #46 (vol. 15 part 3), November 1988

claims.claim: WolfeWiki prints the Fifth Head dedication as 'To Damon Knight, who one well-remembered June evening in 1966 grew me from a bean.'
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, dedication to The Fifth Head of Cerberus, as printed on WolfeWiki
claims.quote: who one well-remembered June evening in 1966 grew me from a bean
claims.page: 'A note about the writing of the story'

claims.feature: other: an editor commissioning the book
claims.claim: Wolfe says Damon Knight, to whom he had sold several short stories, was connected with a publisher and invited him to write a novel.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, undated live chat transcript, SF chat channel (archived by gwern.net under 2015)
claims.quote: he invited me to write a novel for Berkely

claims.feature: other: an editor commissioning the book
claims.claim: Wolfe says Norbert Slepyan of Scribner's heard the title story at the Milford Conference and offered to publish it as a book if Wolfe wrote two more of roughly the same length.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Larry McCaffery, 'On Encompassing the Entire Universe', Science Fiction Studies #46 (vol. 15 part 3), November 1988
claims.quote: Norbert Slepyan of Scribner's was there at that
claims.page: answer on the structure of Cerberus

claims.claim: Gale's Major 21st-Century Writers gives Wolfe's Plant Engineering post as senior editor, 1972-84, agreeing with Ultan's Library against the magazine's own obituary.
claims.source: 'Wolfe, Gene (Rodman)', Major 21st-Century Writers, ed. Tracey Matthews, vol. 5, Gale, 2005
claims.quote: Plant Engineering Magazine, Barrington, IL, senior editor, 1972-84

claims.claim: DeLucci, a Tor colleague, states flatly that David Hartwell was Gene Wolfe's editor for The Book of the New Sun.
claims.source: Theresa DeLucci, 'David Hartwell's Last Gift to Me: Gene Wolfe's Book of the New Sun', Tor.com, 13 March 2017
claims.quote: David was Gene’s editor for The Book of the New Sun
claims.page: body, the World Horror Con 2002 passage

claims.feature: other: an editor's letter as the turning point
claims.claim: The finding aid for the Damon Knight papers says Knight's rejection letters usually suggested how to change the story to make it acceptable, or where else it might be submitted.
claims.source: Joyce Griffith and Stephanie Kays, 'Guide to the Damon Knight papers', Archives West, 2015
claims.quote: usually suggested how to change the story to make it acceptable

claims.feature: other: an editor's letter as the turning point
claims.claim: The finding aid says the Orbit correspondence includes many letters from Gene Wolfe.
claims.source: Joyce Griffith and Stephanie Kays, 'Guide to the Damon Knight papers', Archives West, 2015
claims.quote: Among them: Gene Wolfe, Vonda McIntyre, Gardner Dozois

claims.claim: Kelly reports that In Search of Wonder ends with a 1966 coda in which Knight predicts a split of the field, placing Wolfe among the 'literary' SF writers with Le Guin and Aldiss.
claims.source: Mark R. Kelly, 'Damon Knight, IN SEARCH OF WONDER 3/e', Views from Crestmont Drive, 22 March 2018
claims.quote: ‘literary’ SF (by Le Guin, Aldiss, Wolfe, and others)
claims.page: review body, on the last chapter

claims.claim: Patrick Nielsen Hayden calls Hartwell the field's most consequential editor since John W. Campbell.
claims.source: Patrick Nielsen Hayden, 'David Geddes Hartwell, 1941-2016', Making Light, January 2016
claims.quote: our field’s most consequential editor since John W. Campbell

claims.feature: other: an editor as the whole market
claims.claim: Wolfe says that for years after 'Trip-Trap' the Orbit series was his main market and his other sales were the stories Damon Knight had turned down.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, in conversation with Neil Gaiman, Locus #500, September 2002
claims.quote: were stories that Damon Knight had turned down.

claims.claim: Wolfe says Knight's Milford Writers' Conference was only for published writers, either people he was publishing in Orbit or people he would like to publish in Orbit.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, in conversation with Neil Gaiman, Locus #500, September 2002
claims.quote: either people he was publishing in Orbit or

claims.feature: other: an editor commissioning the book
claims.claim: In the 2002 telling the Scribners editor who commissioned The Fifth Head of Cerberus at Milford is left unnamed, where in 1988 Wolfe named him Norbert Slepyan.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, in conversation with Neil Gaiman, Locus #500, September 2002
claims.quote: would write two more novellas like this, we would

claims.claim: The Locus biographical sidebar gives Wolfe as senior editor of Plant Engineering from 1972 to 84.

claims.feature: other: the record that contradicts the fact
claims.claim: In the 2002 telling Wolfe quotes Pohl's acceptance as 'You know, I think the rewrite has really improved this', where in 1988 he quoted it as 'I'm glad you let me see this again. The re write has really improved it.'
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, in conversation with Neil Gaiman, Locus #500, September 2002
claims.quote: the rewrite has really improved this. I’m glad youlet
